incident_summary.title: Order Service Intermittent 503 Failures
incident_summary.customer_impact: Approximately 18% of checkout requests failing with HTTP 503. Customers unable to complete orders.

most_likely_cause.statement: Scheduled batch job (order-reconciliation) exhausted the shared DB connection pool (20 max), causing DB timeouts and cascading HTTP 503 errors.

alternative_hypotheses.statement: Recent deployment (order-service v2.4.1 at 01:30Z) introduced a performance regression.

evidence_reviewed.description: Scheduled job order-reconciliation started at 02:10 UTC
evidence_reviewed.relevance: Identifies batch job start time near 503 onset

evidence_reviewed.description: Connection pool exhausted (20/20 in use) starting 02:14:30Z
evidence_reviewed.relevance: Direct cause of database connection timeouts

evidence_reviewed.description: DB connection timeout errors escalating to HTTP 503 at 02:15Z
evidence_reviewed.relevance: Links DB pool exhaustion to customer-facing 503 responses

evidence_reviewed.description: Deployment of order-service v2.4.1 completed at 01:30Z with 0 errors for 45 minutes
evidence_reviewed.relevance: Contradicts hypothesis that deployment v2.4.1 directly caused 02:15 incident

recommended_diagnostic_actions: Review API gateway and DB client logs to monitor recovery

actions_requiring_approval.description: Kill or pause the order-reconciliation batch job process
actions_requiring_approval.rationale: Immediately release 16 DB pool connections back to order-service

actions_requiring_approval.description: Restart order-service production replicas to reset connection pool state

conclusion.text: The root cause of the incident is DB connection pool exhaustion caused by the order-reconciliation batch job acquiring 16 of the 20 available pool connections, leaving insufficient connections for API traffic.

limitations: Conflicting evidence present — see alternative hypotheses.
